To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of a standardized, patient-oriented workflow observation tool is feasible and acceptable in emergency departments (EDs); (2) the use of the tool is associated with an increase in the number of patient-oriented tasks observed in the ED; and (3) the use of patient-oriented workflow observation tools can provide a better understanding of the work performed in the ED, and the work performed by individual staff members, than the use of traditional tools.
the patient flow process in hospital EDs is complex and that there are many opportunities to improve the process.
The use of the observation tool in this study was a feasible method for capturing and analyzing patient-oriented workflow in emergency departments.

the development of a patient-oriented workflow analysis method and an observation tool for emergency departments.
the development and testing of an observation tool for studying the workflow of emergency department staff.
the design and implementation of a tool that can help emergency department staff identify and analyze the work that patients do in the department.

patient-oriented workflow in emergency departments is not yet a well-researched area of study.
the use of a structured observation tool for the study of patient-oriented workflow in emergency departments is a feasible method for the collection and analysis of data.
the patient is the central element in the emergency department, and that the emergency department is a patient-oriented environment, where the patient is the centre of the work process.

the patient-oriented workflow in emergency departments is not patient-centered.
